## Constant gravity and the cell form of the gravity work (no `gravity-work` key) {#sec-ch06-cell}

### Summary

The constant-gravity forcing, `const-gravity`[^rg-cf144a647361], adds the body force $\rho g_1$ to the $x_1$ momentum and, in the same
cell, the work $\rho v_1g_1$ to the energy: the cell form of the gravity work. At the pin the cell form is not a
choice, and no key selects it: the `gravity-work` key is gone from the deck, and the face form of @sec-ch06-face
replaces the cell work in every stage. The cell work is still computed, because the forcing that adds the body force adds its work with it; the
hydro then subtracts it and adds the face work. This section states the forcing, the refusal, and why the cell form
is not offered: its work is exact in each cell but its budget does not close, @eq-ch06-cell-defect.

`gravity-work` and `gravity-work-fixer` are the retired `const-gravity` keys: the deck reader refuses them as
unknown, with any value.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The body force of constant gravity and its cell work, @eq-ch06-cell-work; the cell form as a booking is refused.

**Data.** Reads `grav1`[^rg-88e66223cc5e], `grav2`, `grav3`, `non-hydrostatic`[^rg-40de9bc874ef]; writes the momentum rows and, provisionally, the energy row.

**Placement.** Each stage, in the forcing loop; the energy part is replaced later in the same stage (@sec-ch06-face).

**Activation.** `forcing: const-gravity`; no key selects the cell form, and a `gravity-work` key is refused as unknown.

**Guarantee / limits.** The momentum source is exact per cell; the energy is booked by the face form.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch06-cell-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}$[^rg-1186f06fe11f] the `non-hydrostatic` factor (0 to 1) [-]; $G_i$ the hydrostatic-split force
density of @sec-ch05 [N m$^{-3}$]; $W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i$[^rg-c40954ec43ff] and $W^{\mathrm{face}}_i$[^rg-7c89ae1f45ba] the cell and face work densities
[W m$^{-3}$].

| key | meaning | default |
|---|---|---|
| `const-gravity` | the constant-gravity forcing block of `forcing`[^rg-f239edda6399]: $(g_1,g_2,g_3)$ in m s$^{-2}$ | absent: no gravity |
| `non-hydrostatic` | the factor $\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}\in[0,1]$ on the $x_1$ body force and its work | 1 |

: Keys of the `const-gravity` block. {#tbl-ch06-cell-keys}


### Derivation

The forcing books, per cell,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta m_{1,i} &= \Delta t\,\big[\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}\rho_ig_1 + (1-\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}})G_i\big],\\
W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i &= \alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}\,\rho_iv_{1,i}g_1 + (1-\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}})\,v_{1,i}\,G_i ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-cell-work}

the first terms in `ConstGravityImpl::forward_split`
({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityImpl::forward_split >}}) and the $G_i$ terms by the hydrostatic
correction in `HydroImpl::forward` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). Locally the cell
work is exact: the exact gravity work of cell $i$ is $g_1V_i\langle\rho v_1\rangle_{V_i}=g_1V_im_{1,i}$
(@eq-ch06-dwork-template), and $\rho_iv_{1,i}=m_{1,i}$ up to the roundings of the conversion to primitives.

What it gets wrong is the budget. Summed with the potential-energy change of the mass the faces move, it leaves the
defect

$$
\mathcal D = \Delta t\sum_iV_i\big(W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i - W^{\mathrm{face}}_i\big),
$$ {#eq-ch06-cell-defect}

because the face form makes that sum vanish (@eq-ch06-dwork-booked with $P=\mathrm{PE}_d$) and the cell work is a
cell quantity with no partner of opposite sign in the next cell: the mass the faces move is booked at the cell
centres, not where it crosses. `cellface_check.py` `[C2]` measures a defect of $1.6\times10^{-2}$ of
$\sum_iV_i\lvert W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i\rvert$ on a random closed column.[^ch06-cell-chk] Repairing that defect needed a
global fixer (@sec-ch06-fixer); booking the face work instead needs none, which is the design V3 keeps.

[^ch06-cell-chk]: [sha: snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5; deck: the check itself; run:
    `python3 src/snapy_report/ch06/checks/cellface_check.py`, CPU[^rg-7034ba898e85], double, 1 process;
    Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6; output identical to the committed file]. Output `cellface_check.out`, line `[C2]`. The
    port is of the cell work of `ConstGravityImpl::forward` and the face work of `HydroImpl::forward`, whose formulas
    are unchanged at 73c45a7c (`gravity_work_from_face_mass` on Cartesian grids is the same sum written about the
    cell centre); it was not re-run at 73c45a7c.

### Numerical method

The forcing runs inside the stage, with the other forcings, on the stage's primitive state; its increment is scaled
by $\Delta t$ like every other term. Everything is pointwise in the cell. Later in the same stage, once the $x_1$
mass flux is final, the hydro forms the face work and adds `face_gravity_work - original_gravity_work` to the energy
row, `original_gravity_work` being the $W^{\mathrm{cell}}$ of @eq-ch06-cell-work (@sec-ch06-face). The $x_2$ and $x_3$
components of gravity book their cell work and are not replaced. @fig-ch06-cell-defect shows the per-cell terms
whose sum is @eq-ch06-cell-defect.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch06-cell-defect
#| fig-cap: "Per-cell contribution V(W^cell - W^face) to the E + PE_d defect the cell form would leave, on a random closed 24-cell column (nondimensional, g_1 = -10, one stage of length 0.01). The bars do not cancel; booking the face work, as the code does, leaves no such sum."
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of 24 vermillion bars of both signs along x1 from 0 to 1, with a horizontal zero line."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch06.figures.fig_cell_defect import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

**A minimal input.** The gravity block; it has no key for the work, which is booked by the face form:

```yaml
forcing:
  const-gravity:
    grav1: -9.8            # m s^-2
    non-hydrostatic: 1.    # default; 0 to 1
```

**What is refused, and why.** `ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) checks the keys of the
`const-gravity` block (`grav1`, `grav2`, `grav3`, `non-hydrostatic`) with `check_keys` ({{< code src/input/check_keys.cpp check_keys >}}) and refuses:

1. a `non-hydrostatic` factor outside $[0,1]$;
2. any other key, among them the retired `gravity-work` and `gravity-work-fixer`, with the message
   `unknown key 'forcing/const-gravity/<key>'. Valid keys: ...`, whatever the value. The cell form's budget does not
   close (@eq-ch06-cell-defect), so no key offers it, and the fixer that repaired that budget went with it (@sec-ch06-fixer).

The options object has no member for the work form (`ConstGravityOptionsImpl`,
{{< code src/forcing/forcing.hpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl >}}), so `HydroImpl::reset`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}) has nothing to re-check for options built in Python.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| keys, defaults and refusals | {{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `check_keys` | `const-gravity` |
| body force and cell work | {{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityImpl::forward_split >}} | `non_hydrostatic` | `const-gravity` |
| cell work replaced by the face work | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `original_gravity_work` | none: always |

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `gravity-work` and `gravity-work-fixer` are the retired `const-gravity` keys: the deck reader refuses them as unknown,
  with any value, so a deck that still carries them does not load; drop the keys.
- The $x_2$ and $x_3$ components of gravity book cell work only; only the $x_1$ work is replaced by the face form.
:::
